title: Docs: overload errors (429/503), Retry-After guidance, and Hosted vs Dedicated behavior
author: Wei Chen
release_notes: Public docs now define overload-protected error semantics (429/503 + Redwood error codes), recommended client retry/backoff behavior (honor Retry-After, exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries), and clear differences between Hosted and Dedicated overload behavior.
description:
Context: As part of the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding rollout (ENG-4832 / PM-912), customers were seeing mixed 5xx responses during spikes and were unsure whether to retry and how quickly (see SUP-3928 / SUP-3961 / SUP-3974). This PR updates the public docs to: (1) document the overload-protected error taxonomy (HTTP codes + Redwood-specific error codes) and the response shape for both REST and OpenAI-compatible endpoints; (2) recommend a safe retry strategy that avoids retry storms and aligns with our breaker cool-down behavior; (3) clarify what changes (and what does not) for Dedicated capacity compared to Hosted.

What changed (customer-facing): Added a new "Overload protection" page describing why overload shedding exists and how to interpret responses; documented canonical mapping: 429 for admission/edge shedding (client-actionable, retryable) and 503 for temporary capacity unavailability / breaker open (retryable with guidance); added a table of Redwood error codes used for overload (examples: OVERLOADED_ADMISSION, OVERLOADED_CAPACITY, BREAKER_OPEN, QUEUE_LIMIT, MEMORY_PRESSURE) with a short explanation and whether the client should retry; documented required headers: Retry-After (seconds) when retry is recommended, and request-id for support; added OpenAI-compat examples showing how these codes appear in OpenAI-style error objects while preserving standard fields; clarified that overload-protected errors are not billed as successful usage.

Retry guidance (the part most customers will look for): Clients should treat overload-protected 429/503 as retryable only when Retry-After is present; honor Retry-After exactly (do not retry sooner); use exponential backoff with full jitter after the first Retry-After-based retry attempt; cap total retries (recommended default: 3) and cap total retry time (recommended default: 30s) to avoid unbounded tail latency; for streaming requests, reconnecting immediately after disconnect can amplify load—documented a slightly more conservative pattern for SSE/WebSocket-style reconnects and reminded clients to implement jitter; added a small note on idempotency and safe retries (avoid duplicating side effects; retries are safe for inference calls, but callers should handle duplicated downstream writes).

Hosted vs Dedicated: Hosted: may shed early (edge) or in the control/runtime path depending on load; clients should expect occasional 429/503 during regional spikes and use documented retry. Dedicated: still has overload protection, but behavior differs: (a) capacity is isolated to the customer’s pool; (b) shedding is primarily tied to pool saturation / configured autoscaling and queue bounding rather than cross-tenant pressure; (c) Dedicated customers should size concurrency and token budgets appropriately, and should contact support if sustained shedding occurs under expected committed load; updated the docs to state that Dedicated aims for more predictable throughput and provides knobs (autoscaling policy, max concurrency guidance) to minimize overload responses.

Notes/compat: This PR intentionally does not change API behavior; it documents the behavior defined in the error taxonomy work. Language avoids promising exact cooldown durations; we describe Retry-After as the authoritative signal. Also added a short section: "What not to do" (tight retry loops, retries without jitter, parallel retries across regions) based on recent support findings (SUP-3974).

Screenshots/Examples: Included JSON examples for both Redwood REST and OpenAI-compatible error bodies, including Retry-After. All example codes and headers match the shared schema used by SDKs.

Rollout: Docs are written to be accurate pre- and post-rollout by framing overload protection as "may be returned during overload" and pointing customers to the status page / support if errors persist beyond recommended retry caps.

Checklist: [x] Customer-facing error table includes HTTP + Redwood code + retry guidance; [x] OpenAI-compat examples included; [x] Dedicated differences reviewed by PM; [x] Support wording reviewed; [x] Links added to SDK retry helpers and status page; [x] Terminology aligned with Reliability Program ("overload-protected" vs internal failures).

Related: Implementation PRs in platform/runtime (not part of this repo) include standardized overload error payload and headers and SDK surfacing of Retry-After; this PR links to those from the docs where appropriate.

docs(api): document Retry-After + recommended backoff/jitter patterns
docs(openai-compat): add overload error examples for chat/completions/embeddings
docs(dedicated): clarify overload semantics and sizing guidance vs Hosted
docs: terminology pass (overload-protected vs internal 5xx) and cross-links
review_conversation: Henry Cho (PM): Can we avoid hard-coding specific cooldown durations? The canary numbers may change. Also please add one sentence clarifying that Retry-After is authoritative even if the client uses its own backoff policy.

Wei Chen (author): Updated to remove all fixed timing promises; now we only give recommended caps and state that Retry-After must be honored. Added a callout: "If Retry-After is present, do not retry sooner than that value."

Dev Patel (Support): Please add a "What to send support" section (request-id, approximate timestamp, model, region) and make sure we say these are not billed. Also, can we call out the most common misconfig: immediate retries without jitter causing more 429s?
Wei Chen (author): Added a short support escalation section and a "Common client pitfalls" block with the no-jitter retry loop example (based on SUP-3974). Billing note added under the FAQ.
Allison Grant (Observability): In the examples, avoid introducing new header names. Use request-id and Retry-After only. Also watch terminology: "rate limit" vs "load shedding" gets confused.

Wei Chen (author): Confirmed only request-id + Retry-After in examples. Reworded to explicitly distinguish quota/rate limits from overload shedding, and linked to rate-limits doc for 429 that is not overload.

Brian Murphy (API compat): OpenAI-compat example should keep the top-level 'error.type' stable. Add Redwood code as a nested field or in 'error.code' per compat contract; avoid inventing a new top-level field.

Wei Chen (author): Updated OpenAI-compat snippet to keep standard fields, set 'error.code' to Redwood code, and include Redwood-specific details under an 'error.param' note only where already supported. Removed the draft 'redwood_error' field.

Elliot Price (Docs lead): Nice overall. Please add a quick decision tree at the top: 429 with Retry-After vs 429 without Retry-After (rate limit), and 503 with Retry-After. Also add a short note for streaming: reconnect behavior should be more conservative.
Wei Chen (author): Added a decision tree and streaming-specific guidance, including a recommended minimum reconnect delay and jitter note, but still defers to Retry-After when present.
Elliot Price (Docs lead): Approved. Ship it.
